facts.value: ASU offers merit-based scholarships for international first-year and transfer students.
You are automatically considered when you apply for admission — no separate application is needed.
Review scholarship eligibility at ASU’s Scholarship Universe.
You can estimate your total cost using ASU's cost of attendance calculator.
The result includes tuition, housing, meals, health insurance, and personal expenses.
ASU may offer conditional admission to international applicants who meet the academic requirements but who are not proficient in English.

Conditional admission gives international F-1 students three semesters to submit a passing TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE score, or to successfully graduate from ASU Global Launch to be fully admitted to the university.
Applicants who have completed their junior and senior years in a U.S. high school with an SAT EBRW score of 580 taken after April 2016 or an ACT English score of 23.

Applicants who have completed a minimum of 48 transferable semester credits including six credits of freshman English composition at a U.S. college or university with a cumulative GPA of 2.50 or higher.
Applicants holding a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited U.S. college or university.
Applicants who have completed four years of high school in a U.S. high school are subject to high school competency requirements.
TOEFL score of at least 550 (PBT) or 80 (iBT). ASU’s institutional code is 4007.
IELTS overall band score of at least 6.5.
PTE score of at least 60.
Most first-year students live on campus.
You'll apply for housing after paying your enrollment deposit.
Residence halls are assigned by major and campus location.
I-20 delivery option, financial guarantee form, financial document (bank statement or financial support letter), foreign SEVIS address, copy of passport, SEVIS transfer form (if applicable).
All items will show up on My ASU after you are fully admitted.
Processing times for I-20 forms can vary based on when documents were submitted and your admission status.
Your academic credentials must provide information on the courses you took each year and the grades or marks received.
Any document ASU receives becomes the property of the university and will not be returned to you.

Official academic credentials are issued by the registrar of the institution attended, bearing the seal of the institution and registrar’s or academic official’s signature, or verified true copies of credentials by a responsible official of the institution.
All international transcripts must be submitted in the original language accompanied by an official English translation.
Transcripts and supporting documents should be uploaded in My ASU or sent electronically through your school or a transcript service.
For mailing instructions visit admission.asu.edu/apply/transcripts.
